findings.quote: If it equals $1$, then $B = 90^\circ$. One triangle exists.
findings.problem: Step 3 of the SSA procedure says one triangle exists whenever sin B = 1, with no condition on A. It fails when A is 90 degrees or more: A = 150 degrees, a = 1, b = 2 gives sin B = 2(1/2)/1 = 1, so B = 90 degrees and A + B = 240 degrees, and no triangle exists. The angle-sum test in step 5 covers only the step 4 branch, so a student following the numbered steps gets the wrong count. It also contradicts the lesson's own later rule that for A of 90 degrees or more a triangle exists only when a > b (here a < b).
findings.source: Checklist B01; reader-rules boundary test; angle sum of a triangle is 180 degrees (any trigonometry text, e.g. OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e, 10.1, ambiguous case)
